# Public API

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **When a replaceable handler or descriptor carries a security-relevant decision or flag, make it a positional or `required` member, or default it to the safe value. Never make it an optional `init` property that defaults to the permissive value. Set it explicitly on every built-in descriptor.** A replacement handler or a descriptor contributed by a package that never sets the flag silently gets the unsafe default, with no warning at compile time or start-up. For example, private key material ends up treated as public, or logout happens without confirmation. *Check:* Look for new bool or enum members on public result records, descriptors or DTOs built by extension points that control a security check or storage behavior and default to the permissive value through an optional `init` property. <sub>Identity ADR-1380; Identity outcomes of #504; Identity outcomes of #531; Identity outcomes of #554</sub>
- **When a public, replaceable service has to apply a shared policy, especially a security policy, expose that policy as its own public interface seam that replacements resolve. Register its internal default with TryAdd, and keep data-supplying resolvers free of the policy.** If the policy lives only inside the internal default implementation, every replacement has to reimplement it or silently skip it, the copies drift apart, and an extension can't add a bound without replacing the whole service. *Check:* Look for policy logic (combining bounds, enforcing requirements, choosing credentials) that sits only in an internal default of a public replacement point or in a replaceable resolver. Also flag a public concrete default class used as the seam, and a default registered unconditionally. <sub>Identity ADR-1155; Identity ADR-1158; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Make sure an extension seam that takes part in a security decision can only reject or end the operation. It must never skip or weaken a built-in check, change reserved anchoring entries, add a name that was already added, or let the caller pick a path that bypasses a required security step.** Plugins and callers must not be able to break invariants such as callback binding, CSRF checks, allow-lists, reserved identity claims or a required pushed-request channel. *Check:* Look for gate, validator or contributor contracts whose results can override built-in validation, that add or remove claims or fields without checking a reserved list or duplicates, or that expose a public parameter or method letting the caller choose a less secure channel. <sub>Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity ADR-1290; Identity ADR-1275</sub>
- **Model a one-time secret reveal as its own response type (the material-free resource plus the material). Keep read and list resources for secrets metadata-only, and serve any public key half from a separate read-only sub-resource.** With an optional material field on the type every read returns, preventing leaks depends on reviewers catching them. A separate type makes every place a secret can appear visible in the types. *Check:* Look for nullable secret, plaintext, key material, JWK or PEM properties added to a shared resource or list item type, or one response type reused by revealing and non-revealing endpoints. <sub>Identity ADR-1050; Identity ADR-1268</sub>
- **Never expose internal surrogate keys (database identity or snowflake `Id` columns) in API responses, routes or cursors. Expose only the opaque resource identifier.** Only the opaque, server-minted identifier is a public identity. A surrogate key leaks storage details and gets tied to every client. *Check:* Check response models and mappers for a surrogate `Id` property, and check routes for numeric key parameters. <sub>Identity ADR-1014</sub>
- **Don't let a create endpoint's request carry an identifier for the resource it creates. The server mints the identifier and returns it in the `201` body and the `Location` header.** An identifier the caller chooses gets tied to every reference, can never be renamed, and makes every caller handle format, validation and collisions. *Check:* Look for create request DTOs or handlers that read the new resource's id from the body, and for create responses that lack the id in the body or the Location header. Names that are the resource itself, such as a tenant name, are the exception. <sub>Identity ADR-1014</sub>
- **Take a parent resource reference from the route, never from the request body.** Authorization and tenant confinement apply to the route's parent scope, and a value in the body could contradict it. *Check:* Look for request DTOs on nested endpoints that carry a parent id (owner, tenant, resource server) which the handler uses in place of the route value. <sub>Identity ADR-1014</sub>
- **Have a management endpoint that acts on an owner answer 404 for an unknown owner. It must never lazily create resources, such as keys, for that owner.** Get-or-create before the existence check plants state for an owner that doesn't exist. *Check:* Look for get-or-create calls in management handlers that run before the owner's existence is verified. <sub>Identity ADR-1407</sub>
- **In a repository that tracks changes (released, or with a tracked pre-release policy), keep public APIs and the shape of stored or serialized data backward compatible, or ship an explicit migration and a documented breaking change.** Consumers depend on shipped signatures and on data already persisted in the old shape. *Check:* Look for removed or renamed public members, changed signatures, and changed persisted fields, schemas or serialized formats that come with no compatibility path, migration or recorded break. Skip this in a repository whose conventions say it is pre-release and tracks no changes. *Note:* In a repository that is pre-release and tracks no changes, renames and format changes are allowed outright. See the pre-release rule. <sub>Identity .claude/commands/review-code.md; identity-platform .claude/commands/review-code.md; project-template .claude/commands/review-code.md</sub>
- **In a released library, change existing public members only additively. Add a new type, member or overload instead of changing a shipped signature's parameters, return type or nullability.** After release the shipped surface is a consumer contract, and changing a signature, including `string` to `string?`, breaks callers. *Check:* Look for edited public method signatures or nullability annotations, matching edits or `*REMOVED*` lines in PublicAPI.Shipped.txt, and signature changes where an overload would do. This applies only where the repository tracks changes. <sub>Identity ADR-1025; Identity docs/api-compatibility.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **In a released library, remove shipped public surface only in a major version, after it has been marked `[Obsolete("…", error: false)]` and kept working in an earlier minor release. Bump the major version for any removal, signature change, or consumer-visible change in validation or security behavior.** Only additive changes may ship in minor and patch releases, and deprecating first gives consumers time to migrate. *Check:* Look for deleted public types or members (or `*REMOVED*` shipped entries) that weren't marked `[Obsolete]` earlier, and for breaking or behavior-changing diffs without a new major version. This applies only where the repository tracks changes. <sub>Identity ADR-1025; Identity docs/api-compatibility.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **Append new members to a public, serialized or wire enum. Never insert, reorder or renumber existing members.** Reordering or renumbering changes the meaning of values already stored or sent. *Check:* Look for enum diffs that insert members in the middle, reorder them, or change the explicit values of existing members. <sub>Identity ADR-1025; Identity docs/api-compatibility.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **Add a new optional input to a public type, including a positional record or an exception, as a nullable `{ get; init; }` property that the library resolves to a default (failing closed). Never add it as a new or defaulted constructor parameter. Take required inputs as constructor parameters.** A new constructor parameter changes the binary signature, breaks every `new T(...)` call site and serializer, and makes callers pass explicit nulls. Resolving the default inside the library keeps it out of consumer code. *Check:* Look for public constructors or record parameter lists that gain a parameter, especially an optional or nullable one (often visible as call sites now passing `null`), and for `= null` defaults on public constructor parameters. *Note:* Don't ask for `required` on an optional `init` property whose default the library supplies on purpose. <sub>Identity ADR-1025; Identity docs/api-compatibility.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #572; Identity outcomes of #584; Identity outcomes of #724</sub>
- **Don't change what an existing public member accepts or produces while keeping its name and signature. Add a separately named member that says which form it accepts or produces.** Existing callers still compile and run, so a silent change in meaning surfaces only at run time, for example at authentication. *Check:* Look for shared parsing accessors whose accepted inputs widen or narrow, and for public methods whose signature is unchanged but whose stored or returned form changed meaning. <sub>Identity ADR-1123; Identity outcomes of #531</sub>
- **When a property of a public contract becomes nullable, or starts being null on a new call path, document in its XML remarks when it is null, and record the change as the repository's changelog rules require.** Implementers written against the old non-null contract would dereference it and throw. *Check:* Look for public contract properties changed from `T` to `T?`, or newly passed null, without matching remarks and a changelog entry. <sub>Identity outcomes of #600; Identity docs/api-compatibility.md</sub>
- **Where the repository tracks changes, mark a change that breaks callers (a new required constructor parameter, a changed signature) as breaking in its changelog entry, and name who is affected, such as replacement handlers that construct the type. Follow the repository's own rules for where the entry goes and for breaking markers in commit or pull request titles.** Consumers who construct the type or replace a handler get a compile error after upgrading, and the release notes must warn them. *Check:* For public signature changes, check that the changelog entry flags the break and names the affected consumers. An entry goes under `## [Unreleased]` unless the change also sets its own release version, which writes that version's dated section. *Note:* Sources disagree on breaking markers: one repository requires a conventional-commit `!`, another pre-release repository forbids `!` and `BREAKING CHANGE:`. Follow the repository's own rule. Don't ask for extra upgrade or rebuild notes when the package has never been released and the entry already says Breaking. <sub>Identity outcomes of #526; Identity outcomes of #464; identity-platform identity-platform.instructions.md; Identity project-template.instructions.md</sub>
- **In a repository whose conventions say it is pre-release and tracks no changes (for example `pre-release: untracked` in AGENTS.md), make breaking changes as clean cutovers. Don't ask for, and do flag, deprecation steps, `[Obsolete]` forwarding members, compatibility overloads, aliases for renamed settings, readers for older formats, dual paths, migrations, major-version bumps, breaking-change labels, or upgrade, rollback or rollout notes for anything that has only existed in the repository.** Nothing has shipped, so no consumer, package, stored data or token needs protecting. A half-migrated state with two sources of truth is the worse outcome. *Check:* Before raising any compatibility finding (renames, removed settings or registrations, dropped transitive references, tightened nullability, reshaped contracts or stored formats), check the repository's pre-release policy and release status. If it is untracked pre-release, don't report the change, and flag shims kept only for compatibility. <sub>Identity ADR-1025; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity project-template.instructions.md; Identity repository.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #807; Identity outcomes of #702; identity-platform identity-platform.instructions.md</sub>
- **Record every public API change in the project's PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt. Mark removals with a `*REMOVED*` prefix instead of deleting lines from PublicAPI.Shipped.txt, and edit Shipped only at release. Remove stale entries by hand after `dotnet format analyzers`, add both the `extension(Receiver!)` container line and the member line for a C# 14 extension member, and keep the files LF.** PublicApiAnalyzers compares the compiled surface with both files, so the Unshipped diff makes surface changes visible and intentional. The formatter doesn't reliably remove stale entries and may rewrite the files with CRLF. *Check:* Look for public surface changes with no PublicAPI diff, stale entries, missing extension container lines, Shipped edits outside a release, deleted Shipped lines, or whole-file CRLF rewrites. <sub>Identity docs/api-compatibility.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Before a project's first stable release, keep PublicAPI.Shipped.txt holding only `#nullable enable` and record entries in PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt. Don't report churn, renames or removals in the Unshipped file.** Before release the surface isn't a contract, and Unshipped churn is the normal sign of a surface still evolving. A name that appears only in Unshipped has never shipped. *Check:* Flag a pre-release diff that adds entries to PublicAPI.Shipped.txt. Before reporting a rename as breaking, check whether the old name is in Shipped or in a released changelog. <sub>Identity ADR-1025; Identity outcomes of #702</sub>
- **Don't report additions to PublicAPI.Shipped.txt when the pull request is the release commit for that version, or when an already released library is adopting the public API analyzer and the entries match its last released surface.** A release moves Unshipped entries into Shipped, and adopting the analyzer needs a baseline of the shipped surface. Neither is an unreviewed surface change. *Check:* Check whether the version file and changelog show that this PR releases the version and leave Unshipped holding only `#nullable enable`, or whether Shipped is being filled for the first time and matches the last release tag. In the baseline case, at most ask the PR description to call it a baseline. <sub>Buffers outcomes of #112; Buffers outcomes of #23</sub>
- **Don't ask a test project or another non-packable project to add PublicAPI tracking files or to satisfy PublicApiAnalyzers diagnostics.** The analyzers run only where `IsPackable` is not false, because test assemblies have no tracked public surface. *Check:* Check the project's `IsPackable` before reporting missing public API tracking. <sub>Identity ADR-1127</sub>
- **Don't report as semver-major a minor-release change of exception type when the old exception was undocumented and either the input could never succeed or sibling APIs already document the new exception for the same input. Do check that the changelog or a decision record explains why the change ships in a minor release.** Code written against the documentation sees no change, and a major version is kept for changes to documented behavior. *Check:* For a diff that changes which exception is thrown under a minor bump, read the old exception's XML docs and the docs of sibling APIs. Report only if the old exception was documented, or if no changelog or ADR entry records the change. <sub>Buffers outcomes of #112; Buffers outcomes of #96</sub>
- **Keep `assemblyVersion` precision at `major` in version.json, and don't set `AssemblyVersion` by hand. Versions come from the SemVer release, and AssemblyVersion moves only with the major version.** Minor and patch upgrades then drop in as replacements within a major, while different majors load side by side. *Check:* Flag a change to assemblyVersion precision, and AssemblyVersion or Version set in project files or attributes. <sub>Identity ADR-1003; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **Flag a build or versioning change that makes a released library's AssemblyVersion lower than the one its last release shipped with, for example pinning it to Major.0.0.0 after releases shipped the full version.** Consumers compiled against the higher assembly version can fail with FileLoadException, which turns a minor or patch release into a binary break. *Check:* In diffs to versioning properties in props, csproj or version.json, compare the resulting AssemblyVersion with the last release's, and require an explicit override or a changelog note. *Note:* This is the exception to the no-hand-set-AssemblyVersion rule: an explicit `<AssemblyVersion>` in the repository's own props is an acceptable fix here. <sub>NCode.Disposables outcomes of #25</sub>
- **Bump a schema or format version number only for a change to a released version. A field added to a schema that has never shipped belongs in the current unreleased version, with no bump.** A version number tells consumers such as SIEM pipelines that a released shape changed. Versions that count states only the repository ever held protect no one and ship invented history. *Check:* Look for a schema-version constant bumped in a pre-release diff, or docs that describe intermediate unreleased versions. <sub>Identity ADR-1025</sub>
- **In production code, treat every vocabulary (kinds, types, modes, scopes, formats, methods, reasons, statuses, failure codes, audit outcomes and categories, stages) as open. Model it as `public const string` names in a static class, compared ordinally and documented as the known values, or as registered descriptors or strategies resolved by name through a catalog. Don't use a closed enum, a closed switch, or a closed polymorphic `[JsonDerivedType]` list on a base type.** Consumers and sibling packages must be able to add members by registering them, without editing the library. *Check:* Look for new enums, closed lists, exhaustive switches or `[JsonDerivedType]` lists over a vocabulary another package could plausibly extend. Also look for non-ordinal name comparisons, docs that claim the names are exhaustive, and consumers of open codes that have no fallback for unknown names. <sub>Identity ADR-1150; Identity ADR-1119; Identity ADR-1236; Identity ADR-1246; Identity ADR-1278; Identity ADR-1283; Identity docs/audit-records.md; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md; Identity convention-audit.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity repository.instructions.md</sub>
- **In production code, declare an `enum` only when all three hold: its members are fixed by something that can't grow without this library changing (a finite enumeration of an external specification implemented in full, the outcome set of one library-owned operation, or a mirror of a framework type); no other package could ever need another member; and a new member would need a library change anyway.** Closing a vocabulary is the exception. Asking only whether the package owns today's members produced designs that shut out extensions. *Check:* For each new or changed enum, try to state the three-part justification. Flag it if a package other than this one could ever need a member, or if a member is being added for another package's sake. <sub>Identity ADR-1150; Identity convention-audit.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **In production code, never use a `[Flags]` enum, a bitmask, or a `switch` that encodes relationships among a vocabulary's members. Put the relationships in registered descriptors or strategies.** A flags enum closes the bit space and the meaning of every combination, and hard-coded relationships keep the vocabulary closed. *Check:* Grep for `[Flags]`, and for switches or masks over vocabulary members that decide how the members relate. <sub>Identity convention-audit.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **Don't ask to replace an enum with string names, or to make it extensible, when it passes the three-part closed test or a decision record says why it is closed. Examples are an enum that mirrors an RFC-defined finite set or a framework type, lists the options of a library-owned converter, names the only forms the library can import, or is the outcome set of one operation. Don't ask for a throwing default switch arm that earlier validation makes unreachable.** A closed set gains exhaustiveness checking and type safety from an enum. Strings would add validation with no extensibility to show for it, and an unreachable default arm is dead code. *Check:* Before reporting an enum, check where its members come from, whether callers can extend the set, whether an ADR justifies it, and whether validation rejects undefined values before the switch. <sub>Identity ADR-1150; Identity outcomes of #554; Buffers outcomes of #112</sub>
- **Take a hash algorithm as `HashAlgorithmName`, and represent an HTTP status in a public model or error type as `int`, not with a library-defined enum or `HttpStatusCode`.** Both sets are open. The framework already owns the hash vocabulary, and a provider can return a status that `HttpStatusCode` has no member for, which must come through unchanged. *Check:* Look for hashing APIs whose algorithm parameter is an enum or custom type, and for public properties or response models typed `HttpStatusCode`. The enum is fine where an API needs it, such as building an `HttpResponseMessage`. <sub>Identity ADR-1190; Identity review of #320</sub>
- **Don't default to typed name wrappers (such as `readonly record struct Scope(string Name)`) for an open vocabulary. Use `const string` names, and keep wrappers for signatures that would otherwise confuse two name parameters.** A wrapper adds a type per vocabulary without making it any more open. *Check:* Look for new single-string wrapper structs or records introduced for a vocabulary, with no parameter-disambiguation reason. <sub>Identity ADR-1150</sub>
- **In TypeScript shared packages, type a name set that new consumers may extend as the known literals plus `(string & {})`, not as a closed union.** A closed union forces every new app or host to edit the library, while an unknown name can fall back to a default and fail visibly. *Check:* Look for new closed string-literal unions in shared packages for values that a new app or host could add. <sub>Identity ADR-1064</sub>
- **Have an API take the name of an open-vocabulary strategy (such as an encoding) and resolve it through the registered collection, rather than taking a strategy instance.** Settings and stored records carry a name, and resolving it in one place keeps a single point that validates the set. *Check:* Look for public methods that take an encoder or strategy instance where callers would have a configured or persisted name. <sub>Identity ADR-1190</sub>
- **Don't add an empty marker interface. To add an operation that only some implementations support, define a derived interface with real members rather than a base-method parameter that some implementations must reject. For a role that configuration picks by name, resolve the implementation by name through a catalog.** A parameter the base contract doesn't need forces implementations to throw, and a marker interface adds a type without adding a rule. *Check:* Look for new parameters on shared interface methods that some implementations reject with NotSupportedException or ArgumentException, and for new empty interfaces used for capability checks or role tagging. <sub>Identity ADR-1414; Identity ADR-1260</sub>
- **Don't add a capability-specific method to a shared base abstraction such as an audit recorder. Expose one generic entry point that takes a caller-supplied subtype, and let each capability own its event type and a convenience extension method.** A per-capability method stamps one capability's shape onto a general abstraction. *Check:* Look for new methods on a shared interface or base class named after one feature or resource type, and for capability event types or constants declared in the base package. <sub>Identity ADR-1057</sub>
- **Start every type and member at the narrowest visibility that works, and widen it to `public` only for a consumer contract, an entry point, or data that consumers construct. Never widen it so a test can reach it; keep it `internal` and use `InternalsVisibleTo`.** An accidental `public` becomes a contract that must be supported until the next major version. *Check:* Look for new public types or members with no consumer reason, especially members widened alongside new tests that use them. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity csharp-tests.instructions.md</sub>
- **Grant `InternalsVisibleTo` only to the real `*Tests` and `*.Benchmarks` assemblies and to `DynamicProxyGenAssembly2`, never to another production assembly.** Production assemblies must collaborate through public contracts, and coupling through internals bypasses the contract. *Check:* Look for `InternalsVisibleTo` attributes or csproj items that name a production assembly or a test assembly that doesn't exist. <sub>Identity convention-audit.instructions.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity csharp-tests.instructions.md</sub>
- **In production code, make service contracts public interfaces with `internal` `Default*` implementations reached through DI, and make options classes sealed, each with a validator.** Only the interface is the contract. A public implementation class adds surface that consumers would come to depend on. *Check:* Look for public `Default*` or other implementation classes registered in DI, unsealed options classes, and options without a validator. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **Never share one type between two packages that version independently. Keep it in a single owner, or duplicate it on purpose.** A shared type couples independent version lines. *Check:* Look for linked source files, or a type defined in one package and consumed as a contract by an independently versioned one. *Applies to:* `**/*.cs` <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md</sub>
- **Once a type is public in a released package, keep it public and in the package whose capability it is. Don't make it internal or move it to an unrelated package.** Published package IDs and public surface are permanent, and a type belongs with its capability so consumers take a single package pair to get it. *Check:* Look for public types made internal or moved into a package of a different capability. This applies only where the repository tracks changes. <sub>Identity ADR-1500</sub>
- **In production code, make data, options, context, event and result types `sealed`, with get-only or `init` members. Use interfaces only for replaceable DI seams or read-only slices, never for data or persisted records. Pluggability belongs on the store interface.** Data types should be immutable and not extensible by accident, and an interface over a persisted record moves the pluggability seam to the wrong place. *Check:* Look for unsealed data, options or event classes, settable members, and interfaces declared over data or persisted model records. <sub>Identity convention-audit.instructions.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-1051</sub>
- **Keep validation result and similar result types as plain data that consumers and test doubles can construct. Put follow-up operations such as commit or record on the service that produced the result.** Methods on the result would make it hold services and state, and would split the logic across two places. *Check:* Flag result or DTO types that gain methods, or fields holding stores or services, in order to perform follow-up actions. <sub>Identity ADR-1274</sub>
- **Seal a type according to whether it is meant to be derived from, not according to its visibility or testing convenience. Seal public leaf types, keep intended extension bases unsealed, and never leave a class unsealed or `virtual` just so tests can mock it.** Sealing expresses whether derivation is intended, and tests should mock the interface instead. *Check:* Look for unsealed public leaf classes or virtual members justified by mocking, and for intended base types that have been sealed. Before asking for a type to be sealed or deciding it can't be, grep for `:\s*TypeName\b`. A property of that type is composition and doesn't block sealing. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity convention-audit.instructions.md</sub>
- **Use read-only interfaces (`IReadOnlyList<T>`, `IReadOnlyCollection<T>`, `IReadOnlySet<T>`) for parameters and computed return values, and prefer `params IEnumerable<T>` to `params T[]`. Store collection properties as a concrete immutable type such as `ImmutableArray<T>` or a frozen collection, never `IList<T>`, and copy init-assigned collections.** Signatures stay flexible while storage stays concrete and owned. A stored caller list could be mutated after validation, and returning `List<T>` exposes mutable storage that no caller needs. *Check:* Look for `List<T>` or `T[]` parameters and `List<T>` returns that callers only read, interface-typed stored properties, `IList<`, `params T[]`, and validated collections stored without a copy. *Note:* Don't report an internal wrapper that passes arrays unchanged to a client API whose signature requires arrays and never writes to them. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity convention-audit.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #548; Identity outcomes of #554; coordination outcomes of #31</sub>
- **Don't pass or return `null` where an empty form exists. Make a collection parameter non-nullable and have callers pass `[]`, unless null means something different from empty.** Null collections force null-check branches on callers and methods and lead to NullReferenceExceptions. *Check:* Look for methods returning null for collection types, and nullable collection parameters that callers pass `null` to. Confirm that null means nothing different from empty before reporting. <sub>Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity outcomes of #741</sub>
- **Don't make a contract field nullable when every caller would apply the same fallback. Compute the fallback on the server and make the field required.** Otherwise every caller repeats the fallback and some get it wrong. *Check:* Look for new nullable response properties whose docs or callers all substitute the same default. <sub>Identity ADR-1161</sub>
- **When a guard such as `IsConfigured` or `IsValid` guarantees that nullable members are non-null when true, annotate it with `[MemberNotNullWhen(true, nameof(Member))]` so callers read the member directly after the check.** The compiler's nullable analysis then knows what the guard guarantees, so callers need no `!` and no second null check. *Check:* Look for guard properties or methods that sit beside nullable members and lack `[MemberNotNullWhen]` or `[NotNullWhen]`, or callers that use `!` or recheck for null after the guard. *Note:* Don't ask for such a flag to be derived from another member (for example `FailureCode is null`). That getter can't prove the attribute and fails with CS8775, and a private constructor with factories keeps the flag consistent. <sub>Identity review of #833; Identity outcomes of #554</sub>
- **In public API, don't add a `bool` or `enum` parameter whose only job is to switch a method between behaviors, and don't add a mode that makes an existing contract validate a different kind of input. Split them into intention-revealing methods, strategies or contracts. A bool carried as data is fine.** Flag parameters hide intent at call sites and make one contract's requirements conditional on another's. *Check:* Look for public `bool` or `enum` parameters that branch the whole method. Don't report internal members, or a bool passed as a named argument that describes a fact the method reads. <sub>Identity convention-audit.instructions.md; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-1274; coordination outcomes of #31</sub>
- **Pass a growing set of optional selection criteria as a `readonly record struct` with optional `init` properties, and pass paging as a single page-request object (cursor plus limit). Model request, command and validator inputs as init-only request records, with `required` members for required fields. Keep a required identity key that is the operation's subject positional.** Interfaces such as stores are implemented by consumers, so a new positional parameter breaks every implementer and caller. A request object grows without a signature change, while a lone required key gains nothing from a property bag. *Check:* Look for methods gaining another optional filter parameter, separate cursor and limit parameters, positional request or criteria records, validators taking loose parameters, and DTOs that wrap a single required key. <sub>Identity ADR-1080; Identity ADR-1274; Identity csharp.instructions.md; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
